liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let It Grow** (2 reviews): Outstanding version with decisive key changes that weren't always part of that jam; Reviewer calls Let It Grow one of the best, and the following material through the segue great [6][11]
- **Yellow Dog Story** (1 review): Told during technical difficulties; someone, perhaps Mickey, jokes that it's Jerry's birthday, showing the band's playful mood [6]
- **Big River** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Big River a great version, among the first set highlights along with Sugaree [5]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): High Time, Looks Like Rain and Friend of the Devil stand out among the slower first-set ballads [13]
- **Saint Stephen** (1 review): Reviewer finds the second-set St. Stephen sounds phoned in and uninteresting, though Not Fade Away picks up the pace [5]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): Reviewer says The Wheel is rolling well [11]
- Opens the night with high energy alongside Sugaree and Mama Tried, which are played with great force [13]

## Setlist highlights

- **Yellow Dog Story**: back after 210 archived shows (1432 days) [16]

## The recordings

- **gd76-06-23.moore.vernon.15534.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 26 songs; 186 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is bassy and quiet, requiring the volume to be turned up considerably [5]
- **gd1976-06-23.aud.miller.95321.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 23 songs; 182 min; rated 4.57/5 by 7 [2]. Said about its sound: Sounds good for an audience tape; nearly everything is audible clearly and the crowd is enjoying itself; Acoustics clearly indicate a small venue, making the audience recording sound very intimate and lively; Audience sound is mostly good but degraded in a couple of spots; brighter than the other two copies [10][12][14]
- **gd1976-06-23.aud.vernon.6681.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 171 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says this copy is cleaner than other copies: crisp vocals blending with band, Jerry's guitar not overpowering the treble, not too warm [7]

## Around the show

- Judged not as good as the previous night, which the reviewer considers the best show of the run [6]
- Reviewer prefers this version to the other two copies and ranks it among the best of 1976 [11]
- Reviewer, new to 1976, calls this Tower Theatre run their favorite material so far [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd76-06-23.moore.vernon.15534.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jerry Moore; transferred by David Minches; source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-33Ps [1]. Also: Recorded by Jerry Moore from first-row loge with two handheld Sony ECM-33P mics into Sony TC-152 cassette deck, Dolby B on; Analog-to-digital transfer by David Minches, encoded to SHN by Matt Vernon [1]
- **gd1976-06-23.aud.miller.95321.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Unknown Mics -> Master Cassette -> Apogee Ensemble -> Peak -> AIFF [2]. Also: Miller version came from Sony ECM-33P mics to master cassette, with the Moore SHN (15534) patching missing sections [2]
- **gd1976-06-23.aud.vernon.6681.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jerry Moore?; transferred by Matt Vernon; source: Shure mics> Sony TC-152 master cassette > other cassette? > dat's [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Snooky Flowers Grateful Dead: [1976-06-22 Tower Theatre, Upper Darby, PA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1976-06-22-tower-theatre-upper-darby-pa-usa/) [19]
- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1976-06-23 Wed Tower Theater, Upper Darby, PA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1275177302184/grateful-dead-1976-06-23-wed-tower) [23]
